---
title: "Study B — Differential abundance with DESeq2"
subtitle: "Species counts across the three contraceptive arms, adjusted for BV"
format: html
editor: visual
---

We test which bacterial species differ across the three contraceptive arms
(pill, injectable, ring) with **DESeq2**. DESeq2 takes **raw counts** — never
CPM or logged values — and does its own normalisation by estimating a *size
factor* for each sample (roughly, how deeply that sample was sequenced).

This version adjusts for **bacterial vaginosis (`bv`)**: the design is `~ bv + arm`.
Writing `bv` first means DESeq2 estimates the arm effects *on top of* any BV
effect, so a species is called differential only if it differs between arms
beyond what BV status explains. BV is a strong driver of vaginal species like
*Lactobacillus* and *Gardnerella*, so this matters here. The `bv` variable has
three levels (negative, intermediate, positive), with **negative** as the
reference.

Three things we are careful about:

- **Count matrix orientation**: DESeq2 wants features in *rows* and samples in
  *columns*, with columns matching the metadata row order. `read_counts()`
  already guarantees this, and we check it again below.
- **Zeros**: some samples have so few counts that the default size-factor
  method fails on geometric means of zeros, so we use `type = "poscounts"`.
- **Reference level**: DESeq2 compares every arm against the first factor
  level, so we set **pill** as the reference.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8)
source(here::here("R/count_tables.R"))
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(DESeq2)

d <- read_counts("group_b")
meta <- d$metadata
species <- d$species
```

## Set up the DESeq2 object

```{r}
# Counts must be raw integers, features in rows, samples in columns
stopifnot(identical(colnames(species), meta$sample_id))

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(species),          # integer matrix, 220 species x 93 samples
  colData   = meta,                    # one row per sample
  design    = ~ bv + arm               # adjust for BV, then test arm
)

dds$arm <- relevel(dds$arm, ref = "pill")       # arm comparisons are made vs pill
dds$bv  <- relevel(dds$bv,  ref = "negative")   # bv reference is negative status
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = "poscounts")
dds <- DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds)   # the bv and arm comparisons DESeq2 built for us
```

## Results

```{r}
# One results table per contrast, stacked into a single tidy table
# contrast = c(factor, numerator, denominator) — here both arms vs pill
contrast_list <- list(
  "injectable vs pill" = c("arm", "injectable", "pill"),
  "ring vs pill"       = c("arm", "ring", "pill")
)
res_all <- imap(contrast_list, function(contrast, label) {
  as.data.frame(results(dds, contrast = contrast)) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("species") |>
    mutate(contrast = label)
}) |>
  bind_rows()

write.csv(res_all, "Species_Results_bv.csv", row.names = FALSE)

res_all |>
  group_by(contrast) |>
  summarise(
    species = n(),
    significant = sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05),
    up = sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 0),
    down = sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < 0)
  )
```

The full table is saved as `Species_Results_bv.csv` (both contrasts, one row
per species per contrast, with log2 fold change, standard error, p-value and
adjusted p-value).

## Volcano plot

Effect size (log2 fold change) against statistical significance. Species in
the top corners are both large and significant; the red dashed line is the
adjusted p < 0.05 cutoff.

```{r}
volcano <- res_all |>
  mutate(significant = !is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), colour = significant)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_text(
    data = ~ filter(.x, significant, abs(log2FoldChange) > 2),
    aes(label = species), size = 2.6, vjust = -0.5, check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey60", "firebrick")) +
  facet_wrap(~ contrast) +
  labs(title = "Volcano plot — species differential abundance",
       x = "log2 fold change (vs pill)", y = "-log10 adjusted p-value",
       colour = "padj < 0.05") +
  theme_minimal()

volcano
ggsave("figures/volcano_species_bv.png", volcano, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## MA plot

Average abundance (baseMean, x) against fold change (log2, y). Species in grey
were not significant. The spread at low abundance shows why DESeq2 shrinks
fold changes for thinly-sequenced species rather than trusting them.

```{r}
ma <- res_all |>
  mutate(significant = !is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(baseMean, log2FoldChange, colour = significant)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey60", "firebrick")) +
  facet_wrap(~ contrast) +
  labs(title = "MA plot — species differential abundance",
       x = "mean normalised abundance (log scale)",
       y = "log2 fold change (vs pill)", colour = "padj < 0.05") +
  theme_minimal()

ma
ggsave("figures/ma_species_bv.png", ma, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## Top hits

The five most significant species in each contrast:

```{r}
res_all |>
  filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  group_by(contrast) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 5) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(contrast, species,
            log2FC = round(log2FoldChange, 2), padj = signif(padj, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Caveat

Both count tables in this dataset are **compositional**: sequencing depth per
sample is fixed, so "less of species X" can also mean "more of everything
else". DESeq2 models counts as if total reads were free to vary, so treat its
fold changes as relative statements, and read them alongside the
compositional methods (CLR transforms, ordination) from the other modules.

## Choices made

- **Design**: `~ bv + arm`; BV is adjusted for because it is a strong driver
  of vaginal species composition. Alternatives are the simpler `~ arm`, or a
  richer design also including `nugent` (which is nearly the same information
  as `bv` and would risk collinearity).
- **Reference level**: pill; injectable would be DESeq2's default otherwise.
- **Size factors**: `type = "poscounts"` because species counts contain many
  zeros; the default geometric-mean method can fail on all-zero samples.
- **Contrasts**: injectable vs pill and ring vs pill; an alternative is
  a likelihood-ratio test of the whole arm term at once.
- **Significance threshold**: adjusted p < 0.05 (Benjamini–Hochberg, DESeq2's
  default); no fold-change cutoff was added.
- **No species pre-filtered** before DESeq2; filtering very low-count species
  is an alternative that changes little here (only 220 species).
- **Counts were rounded to integers** to satisfy DESeq2's input requirement.
- **Compositional caveat accepted**: fold changes are interpreted as relative,
  not absolute, changes.
